BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to request removal. 
Email: mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com

The suspect, identified as Francisco Martinez, was already on extended supervision from the previous time he was convicted of OWI, where he pled guilty to a hit and run, causing the death of 30-year-old Curtis Bond's. At the time of his arrest, Martinez was found unconscious at the wheel with his six-year-old son still in the car, and Bond's blood on the hood. He was sentenced to five years in state prison and was on his first year of extended supervision during the events of this video. Martinez was charged with two felony counts of fleeing and eluding an officer, an OWI, his fourth time being charged with operating a vehicle while intoxicated. He was also charged with three misdemeanors, resisting an officer, operating while revoked, and failure to install an ignition interlock device in his vehicle. Martinez entered a plea agreement with the court, where his misdemeanors were dropped and the fleeing and eluding charge was dismissed but read in, in exchange for pleading guilty to OWI. He was given one year in prison and one year of extended supervision while his license was revoked for three years. Martinez was later charged and pled guilty to refusing to submit to alcohol testing after his arrest. He is currently serving the remainder of his sentence with the Wisconsin Department of Corrections and is eligible for extended supervision in December 2026.
